intro: In İstanbul province stands Pera Museum, a private museum opened in 2005. It is known for its Orientalist painting collection, and it is the home of Osman Hamdi Bey's 'The Tortoise Trainer'.
history: Founded by the Suna and İnan Kıraç Foundation, the museum opened in 2005 in the Bristol Hotel building of 1893. At the heart of its collection are the works of European painters who depicted the Ottoman world between the seventeenth and twentieth centuries, together with the paintings of Osman Hamdi Bey.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the Orientalist painting collection and 'The Tortoise Trainer', then the Anatolian weights and measures and the Kütahya tiles.
facts: Did you know? Osman Hamdi Bey's 'The Tortoise Trainer' was bought at a record price in 2004, and it has been the museum's emblem ever since. The building has a past of its own: the museum occupies the Bristol Hotel building of 1893, its façade kept and its interior rebuilt entirely as gallery space.
outro: This brings our tour of Pera Museum to an end. Please leave the objects untouched and take your photographs without flash. Take a last look at the paintings before you step back into the street. Enjoy your visit.
